name: Incremental review of a minimal push

summary: Projector's review loop (start-review-loop) watches the operator's pull requests and gives every pushed head a review. Each review runs the full method: it reads every changed file, runs the repository's checks, and posts a long review body. A push that changes one padding value on a pull request that already had a clean review pays the same cost, and its reader scans hundreds of words for a two-line change.

This pull request lets the loop publish an incremental review instead: a short clean verdict on the new head that names the loop's last full review of the pull request and reads only the change since that review's head. It implements the plan in docs/projects/incremental-review/readme.md.

1. Measure the change. project review interdiff <number> finds the full review in the loop's record and diffs the pull request's own change since that head. When the merge base moved, because the author merged or rebased onto the base branch, it first replays the reviewed head onto the new merge base with git merge-tree, so the base branch's own changes stay out of the patch.
  2. Check the rules a read cannot see. The same command refuses unless incremental reviews are on, a loop runs the review, the head is trusted, the loop's newest verdict is a clean one on another head, the full review came from the same Projector version, model, and effort, no finding is open, the change can be measured, every file in it is readable text, and, after a moved merge base, a project review gate run passed on this head.
  3. Decide by reading. The reviewer reads every line of the patch and asks whether the full method would catch something this read cannot. Any doubt, or any refusal, means a full review.
  4. Publish. project review publish --incremental checks the rules again and posts a clean COMMENT with a lead that links the full review and states the change's size.

The site's page header shows such a review as Clean · incremental from <sha>, linking the full review. The plan stays in-progress: unit tests prove its criteria 1 to 4, and criterion 5, a run of a live loop against a scratch repository on GitHub, has not run.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Full review: a review that runs the whole method in skills/review-pr/method.md.
  • Incremental review: a short clean verdict that builds on the loop's last full review.
  • Loop record: loops/<id>/published.json in Projector's state directory, one entry per review the loop published.
  • Merge base: the commit the pull request's diff is taken from. O and MO are the full review's head and merge base. N and MN are the new head's.
  • Interdiff: the pull request's own change from O to N.
  • Gate: the repository's check command, review.gate, which project review gate runs and records.

cards.title: How the head moved (kind)
cards.html:
KindWhen
pushO is an ancestor of N, and the merge base did not move.
mergeAncestor, and a merge commit since O brought in the new merge base.
retargetAncestor, and the merge base moved with no such merge, as after a stacked parent squash-merges.
rebaseNot an ancestor, and the merge base moved.
rewriteNot an ancestor, and the merge base did not move, as after an amend.

The kind labels the move. No rule reads it.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html: The Projector reviews of b6980ec and d9186a3 are both clean with no finding threads. The newest head merges main, resolving a conflict in one import line, and takes both suggestions from the first review: one phrase per kind of move in KINDS, shared by the command output and the lead, and a rewrapped paragraph in skills/start-review-loop/SKILL.md.

groups.title: Measuring the change and checking the rules
groups.kicker: project review interdiff: the interdiff, its kind, and the rules a read cannot see
intro: project review interdiff answers two questions before a reviewer reads anything. What did the pull request itself change since the loop's last full review? And do the facts a reader cannot see allow an incremental review at all?

A plain git diff O N would also count what a merge or rebase brought in from the base branch. So when the merge base moved, measure replays O's change onto the new merge base with git merge-tree --merge-base=MO MN O and diffs that tree against N. A conflicted replay keeps diff3 markers in the file, so the patch shows the conflict region leaving and the author's resolution arriving. MO comes from the loop record, not from git merge-base, because that command gives the wrong commit after a stacked parent is rewritten.

incremental_rules then refuses at the first rule that fails, and interdiff and publish --incremental both call it. The gate rule is last, so a refusal that names it means every other rule passed. Its needs_gate flag tells the reviewer to read first and run the gate only when the read decides for an incremental review.

checks.text: The review ran the 605 unit tests at this head, all passing. The tests build real Git histories in temporary repositories for each kind, for conflicted rebases and merges, for a stack cascade, and for a Git without merge-tree --merge-base.

files.note: measure, incremental_rules, the incremental marker and lead, and publish --incremental.

checks.text: The replay runs in the operator's checkout. merge-tree writes objects only, and touches neither the working tree nor the index, so uncommitted work stays as it is.
A moved merge base with O still an ancestor is a merge only when a merge commit since O contains the new merge base. Otherwise it is a retarget.
Each kind maps to one phrase. interdiff prints it, and the incremental lead puts it after "across a" for every kind but a push, so a new kind needs a phrase that reads both ways.
A record entry with no base, as an earlier release wrote, refuses as unmeasurable. test_a_record_without_the_full_reviews_merge_base_cannot_be_measured covers it, and the review ran it.

After a moved merge base, the rule requires a gate record whose sha is this head and whose exit code is 0. setup writes a fresh state, so a gate from an earlier review cannot count. The tests the review ran cover a failed gate, a gate on an earlier head, and an empty interdiff across a moved base.
Publish applies the rules again to the live state, after the head check and the collision check, so a thread opened since interdiff ran still refuses.
Every loop record entry now stores base, the merge base a later interdiff measures from, and from, which marks an incremental review that a later one never builds on.

checks.text: An unset key means on. A value that is not a boolean raises a ConfigError naming the key, so both commands exit non-zero and the head gets a full review.

groups.title: Showing an incremental review on the site
groups.kicker: The page header names the full review an incremental review builds on
intro: Each summary page's header shows the verdict of the newest Projector review of its head. review_statuses now reads each review body through verdict_marker, which also reads the projector-incremental line directly after the marker. A clean incremental head gains incrementalFrom: the full review's head and that review's URL.
The review marker itself is unchanged, so a site built by an earlier release still matches it and shows plain Clean.

groups.title: Telling the reviewer when to review incrementally
groups.kicker: The review-pr and start-review-loop skills, and the CLI reference
intro: The code enforces facts, and the skill carries the judgment. review-pr gains a section, "Review a minimal push incrementally", with the deciding question, the kinds of change that usually qualify, and the rule that any refusal or doubt means a full review.

Prose qualifies only when a full review would pass it. So the skill tells the reviewer to read changed documentation against the code it describes, and each changed comment against guidelines.md § 1. Text an agent follows, such as a SKILL.md, never counts as prose.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Real Git histories against the fake GitHub, and the header under node
intro: tests/test_review.py adds an IncrementalCase that publishes a clean full review in a temporary repository, then builds each next head with real Git: a push, a merge, a rebase, a conflict, an amend, a stack cascade, and a retarget. tests/test_site.py covers review_statuses and renders the header under node.
